heading: INT. FUNERAL RECEPTION - COMMUNITY HALL - DAY

units.text: INT. FUNERAL RECEPTION - COMMUNITY HALL - DAY
Trays of sandwiches, a slideshow looping on a projector.
Coach Frank Dunleavy's face, forty years of whistles and clipboards, fills the wall.
Two teenagers in oversized suits fight over the last deviled egg while a waiter weaves past them with a tray of lukewarm coffee and a little brown dog sneaks under the buffet table.
Ray Pruitt, 50s, former star pitcher, stands by the window with a paper cup.
Across the room Luis Navarro, 50s, his old catcher, enters, spots him, and stops dead.
INSERT - THE SLIDESHOW
A photo of both men, young, arms around each other, a championship trophy between them.
BACK TO SCENE
Luis crosses the room slowly.
Ray doesn't turn.
You came.
units.name: LUIS

units.text: He was my coach too.
units.name: RAY

units.text: He was his coach more than he was yours. After what you did to him he barley spoke your name.
units.name: LUIS

units.text: What I did to him. Okay.
units.name: RAY

units.text: CLOSE ON Ray's hand tightening around the cup, coffee spilling over his knuckles.
You threw that game. Everybody knew. Frank knew. he took it to his grave and so did I untill today.
units.name: LUIS

units.text: You want to do this at his funeral.
units.name: RAY

units.text: You wanted to do it at his funeral. You wore the ring.
units.name: LUIS

units.text: A teenager drops a plate.
The waiter freezes.
The dog yips.
The whole room turns, and the slideshow flips to the next photo, Frank holding a trophy over his head.
I'm sorry.
units.name: RAY

units.text: Say it to him.
units.name: LUIS
paren: blinking, his anger leaving all at once

units.text: Ray sets the cup on the sill, walks to the projector, and stands in its beam so Frank's smile falls across his chest.
